title: Cofibrant simplicial homotopy groupoids and degreewise completion
statement: Use simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], geometric realization and path components [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and weak homotopy equivalences and Kan fibrations [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Fix a small set $O$. A simplicial category $A$ on $O$ has simplicial mapping sets $A(a,b)$ for $a,b\in O$, associative simplicial composition and identity vertices. Write $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ for these categories and functors fixing $O$, equipped with the fixed-object model structure from the $O\times O$-sorted theory of composition and units [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model]: weak equivalences and fibrations are detected on every mapping simplicial set. Cofibrant means that the map from the identity-only category on $O$ has the left lifting property against every mappingwise trivial Kan fibration. The ordinary category $\pi_0A$ has objects $O$ and morphisms $\pi_0(|A(a,b)|)$. Suppose that $A$ is cofibrant and every morphism of $\pi_0A$ is invertible. Define $A[A^{-1}]$ by groupoid-completing the ordinary category of degree-$n$ arrows of $A$ in each degree $n$, adjoining formal inverses to all arrows and imposing the composition and inverse relations; the simplicial operators are induced by the universal properties. Then the canonical object-preserving simplicial functor $A\to A[A^{-1}]$ is a weak homotopy equivalence on every mapping simplicial set. No Kan condition on the mapping sets and no connectedness or nonemptiness assumption on $O$ or on individual mapping sets is imposed.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories, Proposition 9.5 (the if direction), printed p.280; fixed-object weak equivalences in 1.4(v), completion in 9.1, and model structure in 7.2. Also the explicit use of [4, 9.5] in Bergner, A model category structure on the category of simplicial categories, Lemma 4.1, printed p.14. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopy theorem.

proof.text: Put $G=A[A^{-1}]$ and $j:A\to G$. Let $R=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$ from [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products], and apply it to every mapping set, using its canonical finite-product comparisons to define composition and identities. This constructs simplicial categories $C=RA$, $D=RG$ and an object-preserving functor $f=Rj:C\to D$. All their mapping sets are Kan, and the natural maps $A\to C$ and $G\to D$ are mappingwise weak equivalences. They identify the categories of components, so $\pi_0C$ is a groupoid. The inverse operations of $G$ are simplicial maps $G(a,b)\to G(b,a)$; applying $R$ and its product comparisons preserves both inverse equations, so $D$ is itself a degreewise simplicial groupoid. No cofibrancy of $C$ or $D$ is claimed or needed.

source.place: Proposition 9.5, if direction: preliminary functorial local Kan replacement, an agent expansion avoiding a fibrancy assumption.

proof.text: Use the bisimplicial nerve $B(V)$ and $NV$ defined in [lem-coef-cofibrant-completion-nerve-equivalence]. That node applies to the original cofibrant $A$ and gives $Nj:NA\to NG$ as a weak equivalence. The units give $NA\to NC$ and $NG\to ND$ as weak equivalences as well. Here are the details for this assertion: at fixed nerve degree $p$ each map is a disjoint union of finite products of mapping-set unit maps. Realization preserves finite products and coproducts by [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. Components of a finite product are products of components; based cubical maps and their homotopies into a finite product are tuples, so its based homotopy groups are products. In a disjoint union every path or based cube remains in its summand. Thus these row maps are weak equivalences, also when a factor or the index set is empty. Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence]. The natural square with horizontal maps $Nj,Nf$ and these unit maps commutes, since all maps are induced on strings of arrows. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] gives $Nf:NC\to ND$ a weak equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 9.5, final appeal to Proposition 9.2, with the Kan-replacement nerve comparison expanded.

proof.text: For a vertex $u\in C(a,b)_0$, choose a vertex $v\in C(b,a)_0$ representing its inverse in $\pi_0C$. The composites $vu,uv$ and the respective identities are joined by paths in the realizations of the endomorphism sets. Composition with these paths gives homotopies between precomposition by $vu$ (respectively $uv$) and the identity on $|C(a,y)|$ (respectively $|C(b,y)|$), because realization respects products by [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. Therefore precomposition $u^*:C(b,y)\to C(a,y)$ and $v^*$ realize to homotopy inverses. Apply [lem-coef-homotopy-equivalence-weak] to see that $u^*$ is a weak equivalence, for every $y$. The same assertion for $D$ follows already from its strict inverses. A component of a nonempty simplicial set contains a vertex: every point in a realized simplex is joined to one of its vertices. Thus the chosen inverse class has a vertex representative. Empty mapping sets present no exception to the argument: precomposition maps with two-sided homotopy inverses are equivalences between the empty sets when either side is empty.

source.place: Proposition 9.5, hypothesis that the component category is a groupoid: spell out its implication for composition actions.

proof.text:
Fix $y\in O$ and let $V$ denote either $C$ or $D$. Define a bisimplicial set
$$E(V,y)_{p,q}=\coprod_{x_0,\ldots,x_p\in O}\left(\prod_{i=1}^{p}V(x_{i-1},x_i)_q\right)\times V(x_p,y)_q.$$
In the nerve direction drop the first arrow, compose adjacent arrows, or compose the last arrow with the final $V(x_p,y)$ entry; degeneracies insert identities. The mapping-set operators act on every entry. Associativity and units give the simplicial identities; the two directions commute since composition and identities are simplicial. Forgetting the final entry gives $p_\bullet:E(V,y)_{\bullet,\bullet}\to B(V)_{\bullet,\bullet}$. In each nerve degree both objects are Kan complexes: products and disjoint unions of Kan complexes fill horns coordinatewise in the summand selected by the horn. The map $p_p$ is a Kan fibration, being on each summand a projection with Kan fiber $V(x_p,y)$. These claims include empty fibers, because a lifting square for a horn in such a fiber has no top map; all horns are nonempty. The fiber of $p_0$ over $x\in O=B(V)_{0,0}$ is exactly $V(x,y)$.

source.place: Proposition 9.5, construction of N(V,V), restricted to its component labelled y; explicit bisimplicial bar and projection.

proof.text:
For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, compare the naturality square of $p_n,p_m$ with its strict pullback $P=B(V)_{n,\bullet}\times_{B(V)_{m,\bullet}}E(V,y)_{m,\bullet}$. All three spaces over $B(V)_{n,\bullet}$ are Kan and both projections are Kan fibrations. Over a vertex represented by $x_0\xrightarrow{u_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{u_n}x_n$, the map $E(V,y)_{n,\bullet}\to P$ on strict fibers is
$$V(x_n,y)\longrightarrow V(x_{\alpha(m)},y),\qquad h\longmapsto h\circ u_n\circ\cdots\circ u_{\alpha(m)+1}.$$
For $\alpha(m)=n$ the composite is the identity. Step 3 makes every such map a weak equivalence. For Kan fibrations these strict fibers compute homotopy fibers, by the homotopy-pullback model in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] with the identity base map to conclude $E(V,y)_{n,\bullet}\to P$ is a weak equivalence. Thus every naturality square is a homotopy pullback. All hypotheses of [lem-coef-equifibered-bisimplicial-diagonal] now hold, and its natural fiber comparison gives
$$V(x,y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{hofib}_x\bigl(\operatorname{diag}E(V,y)\longrightarrow NV\bigr).$$
This comparison is natural for $f:C\to D$, since the bar map applies $f$ to every displayed arrow and preserves the object label $x$. Diagonals need not be Kan: the cited theorem computes their homotopy fibers after functorial Kan replacement.

source.place: Proposition 9.5, bar quasifibration argument; replace the appeal to May Theorem 7.6 / Section 12 by the existing equifibered-diagonal theorem, verifying its hypotheses.

proof.text: For fixed $q$, $E(V,y)_{\bullet,q}$ is the ordinary nerve of the slice category $V_q/y$: its objects are arrows $x\to y$ and a morphism from $a:x\to y$ to $b:z\to y$ is $t:x\to z$ with $bt=a$. A chain in this slice is uniquely a chain $x_0\to\cdots\to x_p$ together with its last arrow $x_p\to y$, exactly the displayed bar formula. This slice has terminal object $1_y$. The unique map of each object to $1_y$ is a natural transformation from the identity to the constant functor, so [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence] makes its nerve weakly contractible. The theorem applies to each small category $V_q/y$, without any invertibility condition on those slice arrows. Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] in the exchanged direction to obtain $\operatorname{diag}E(V,y)\to *$ a weak equivalence. In particular the bar map $\operatorname{diag}E(C,y)\to\operatorname{diag}E(D,y)$ is a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

source.place: Proposition 9.5: the components of N(V,V) are contractible, expanded through the degreewise terminal slice categories.

proof.text: Apply functorial Kan replacement to the commutative square of bar projections for $C,D$. The maps on total spaces are weak equivalences by step 6 and those on bases by step 2; their replacements are weak equivalences by naturality of the unit and two-out-of-three. The point maps selecting $x$ agree because $f$ fixes $O$. Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to the cospans $R\operatorname{diag}E(C,y)\to RNC\leftarrow *$ and $R\operatorname{diag}E(D,y)\to RND\leftarrow *$. It gives a weak equivalence of their homotopy fibers at $x$. The natural comparisons in step 5 form a commuting square whose top map is the actual $f_{x,y}:C(x,y)\to D(x,y)$ and whose other three sides are weak equivalences. Consequently $f_{x,y}$ is a weak equivalence. Finally naturality gives $f_{x,y}\eta_{A(x,y)}=\eta_{G(x,y)}j_{x,y}$. Both unit maps are weak equivalences by [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products], so two-out-of-three gives the required weak equivalence for the canonical $j_{x,y}$ itself. This proves every mapping-set assertion. If $O$ is empty there are no pairs to check; if $O$ is disconnected the argument is made separately at the specified vertex $x$ and permits empty homotopy fibers throughout.

source.place: Proposition 9.5, final comparison with the completed groupoid; explicit natural homotopy-fiber comparison and removal of the auxiliary Kan replacement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q31-3060e50b2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node lem-coef-cofibrant-completion-nerve-equivalence and the statement of every cited node in full. The item statement is unchanged and correct. It is DK 9.5 (if direction); its definition of cofibrancy is the LLP of I_O, the initial object of the sorted-algebra model. Edge cases checked: O empty, empty mapping sets, a simplicial group, and a resolution of the monoid N, where the hypothesis fails. It involves no base-change morphism or coefficient category and does not change the route. I checked all seven steps. Step 1: Ex^inf preserves finite limits, so D keeps strict inverses and pi0 C is a groupoid. Step 2: product and coproduct invariance through k-products, the diagonal lemma, then two-out-of-three for Nf. Step 3: the composition order is right (u*v* = (vu)*), and the homotopy is continuous because [0,1] is compact Hausdorff. Step 4: the bar faces are right (d_p gives h∘u_p), rows are Kan, and the projections are Kan fibrations, also with empty fibers. Step 5: the tail-composite fiber map is right; with fiber detection for the identity base, every square is a homotopy pullback, and all hypotheses of the equifibered-diagonal node hold. Step 6: the column is N(V_q/y), contracted through the terminal object 1_y and the natural-transformation node. Step 7: pullback invariance plus naturality give f_{x,y}, then j by two-out-of-three. proof_deps is the union of uses, all lemmas are in the same unit, and there are no tool_uses. The new node is DK 9.2 and is true: free category and free groupoid nerves are both weakly equivalent to the graph, then the diagonal lemma and a retract give the cofibrant case. It is strictly weaker than the item, not one of its clauses. It is statement-only and self-contained, with five real searches and a correct blueprint from/via. My DAG search found no duplicate. Computing the dependency closures confirms that the free-category-nerve, free-calculus and simplicial-inversion nodes all reach the item, so citing them would close a cycle; the item is acyclic.
